# OpenDroneKit SDK reference

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_sdk_reference.py from the code's signatures and
     docstrings. Do not edit by hand: change the docstring and regenerate. -->

SDK version **1.0.0**, plugin API level **1.1**.

Everything on this page is public API under semantic versioning: a breaking change
bumps the SDK's major version (or, for the plugin contracts, the plugin API major
level). Names not listed here, modules starting with an underscore, and the packages
behind the SDK (`app`, `core`, `mission`, `sdk`) are internal and may change in any
release. Start with the [quickstart](README.md).

Contents: [opendronekit](#opendronekit) · [opendronekit.plugins](#opendronekitplugins)

## opendronekit

OpenDroneKit Python SDK.

A stable, typed layer over the OpenDroneKit core: open or create a project, plan and
export a mission, run a reconstruction, detect, measure and write a report -- through
the same code the desktop application runs::

    import opendronekit as odk

    with odk.Workspace("odk-data") as ws:
        project = ws.create_project("Aukerman")
        plan = project.plan_mission(aoi, template="grid", altitude_m=70)
        plan.export(["qgc_plan", "kml"])
        project.import_dataset("odm_aukerman/images")
        recon = project.reconstruct(engine="auto")
        report = project.generate_report(title="Aukerman survey")

Versioning: ``__version__`` follows semantic versioning. Everything listed in
``__all__`` (and the names documented in ``docs/sdk/reference.md``) is the public API;
a breaking change to it bumps the major version. Modules and names starting with an
underscore, and everything outside the ``opendronekit`` package, are internal.

The plugin API is :mod:`opendronekit.plugins` (contract level ``PLUGIN_API_LEVEL``).

| Constant | Value |
|---|---|
| `opendronekit.__version__` | `'1.0.0'` |

### `opendronekit.CrackDetection`

*dataclass* `opendronekit.CrackDetection(image: Path, source: str, model_used: str, model_key: str, model_sha256: str, crack_pixels: int, crack_ratio: float, length_px: float, max_width_px: float, mask_path: Path, overlay_path: Path)`

### `opendronekit.MissionPlan`

*class* `opendronekit.MissionPlan(project: 'Project', plan: dict[str, Any], summary: MissionSummary, geojson: dict[str, Any])`

A planned mission: its summary, its GeoJSON and the full plan, ready to export.

#### `opendronekit.MissionPlan.save(name: str = '', note: str = '') -> dict[str, Any]`

Save this plan as a new version in the project's mission history.

#### `opendronekit.MissionPlan.builtin_formats() -> list[str]`

The mission export formats built into OpenDroneKit (plugins not included).

#### `opendronekit.MissionPlan.export(formats: Iterable[str] | None = None, *, directory: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None, stem: str | None = None) -> dict[str, list[Path]]`

Write the mission in each format; returns ``{format: [files]}``.

Built-in formats are those of :meth:`builtin_formats`; any other name is looked
up as an installed exporter plugin. A format that fails raises (built-in) or
raises :class:`PluginError` (plugin) -- a file is never reported that was not
written.

### `opendronekit.Project`

*class* `opendronekit.Project(workspace: Workspace, project_id: int)`

One project in a :class:`Workspace`. Obtain it from the workspace, not directly.

#### `opendronekit.Project.info` *(property)*

This project's row in the workspace index (refused if it was deleted).

#### `opendronekit.Project.name` *(property)*

The project's name.

#### `opendronekit.Project.root` *(property)*

The project's folder on disk.

#### `opendronekit.Project.audit_log(limit: int = 200) -> list[dict[str, Any]]`

The project's audit trail, newest first (up to ``limit`` events).

#### `opendronekit.Project.plan_mission(aoi_lonlat: Sequence[LonLat], *, template: str = 'grid', **options: Any) -> MissionPlan`

Plan a mission over an area of interest.

``aoi_lonlat`` is a polygon as ``[[lon, lat], ...]``. ``template`` is a built-in
planner template (see :meth:`Workspace.mission_templates`) or
``"plugin:<name>"`` for an installed mission-template plugin, which is then
called with ``aoi_lonlat`` and ``options`` and returns the planner options.
Other ``options`` are the planner's: ``altitude_m``, ``front_overlap_pct``,
``side_overlap_pct``, ``speed_m_s``, ``camera``, ``gimbal_tilt_deg`` ...
An unknown template is refused rather than silently planned as a grid.

#### `opendronekit.Project.import_dataset(folder: str | os.PathLike[str], name: str = '') -> Dataset`

Register an image folder with the project and make it the active dataset.

#### `opendronekit.Project.reconstruct(images: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None, *, engine: str = 'auto', profile: str = 'standard', max_image_size: int | None = None, dense: bool | None = None, use_gpu: bool = True, epsg: int | None = None, output_dir: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None, timeout_s: float | None = None, progress: Progress | None = None, poll_s: float = 0.5) -> Reconstruction`

Run a reconstruction and wait for it.

``images`` defaults to the active dataset (:meth:`import_dataset`). ``engine``
is ``auto``, ``colmap`` or ``custom``. Raises :class:`Refused` before starting
(no images, a busy output folder...) and :class:`JobFailed` if the job fails;
a :class:`TimeoutError` cancels the job.

#### `opendronekit.Project.detect_cracks(image: str | os.PathLike[str], *, use_model: bool = True, min_area_px: int = 30) -> CrackDetection`

Segment cracks on one photograph; the mask and overlay are saved in the project
under ``analysis/cracks/<image stem>/<source>/``.

With ``use_model`` the installed ``crack_segmentation`` model runs; when it is
not installed the classical heuristic runs instead and the result says
``source="heuristic"``. Pass ``use_model=False`` to ask for the heuristic.

#### `opendronekit.Project.run_model(model_key: str, image: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> Detections`

Run any installed registry model on one image (refused if not installed).

#### `opendronekit.Project.detect(image: str | os.PathLike[str], *, detector: str) -> Detections`

Run a detector plugin (``detector="<plugin name>"``) on one image.

#### `opendronekit.Project.measure_image(kind: str, image: str | os.PathLike[str], pixels: Sequence[Sequence[float]], *, scale_mm_per_px: float | None = None, reference_pixels: Sequence[Sequence[float]] | None = None, reference_length_mm: float | None = None, label: str = '') -> Measurement`

A distance or area on one photograph of the active dataset.

A photograph has no scale of its own: give ``scale_mm_per_px`` or a reference of
known length (``reference_pixels`` + ``reference_length_mm``). Without either
the measurement is refused.

#### `opendronekit.Project.measure_crack(image: str | os.PathLike[str], mask: str | os.PathLike[str], *, scale_mm_per_px: float | None = None, reference_pixels: Sequence[Sequence[float]] | None = None, reference_length_mm: float | None = None, label: str = '') -> Measurement`

Crack length (mm) from a crack mask over a dataset photograph; needs a scale.

#### `opendronekit.Project.measure_map(kind: str, coordinates_lonlat: Sequence[LonLat], *, raster: str | os.PathLike[str] = '', **options: Any) -> Measurement`

Measure on the project's georeferenced rasters (the map's Measure tool).

``kind``: distance, area, perimeter, slope, profile, volume, cut_fill or
stockpile. ``raster`` defaults to the project's orthomosaic (or DSM).

#### `opendronekit.Project.measurements() -> list[dict[str, Any]]`

Every measurement recorded in this project, as stored.

#### `opendronekit.Project.report_readiness(report_type: str = 'standard') -> dict[str, Any]`

The report checklist for ``report_type``: what the project holds, what is
missing and the warnings the report would carry.

#### `opendronekit.Project.generate_report(*, title: str = 'Inspection report', report_type: str = 'standard', formats: Sequence[str] = ('html',), author: str = '', organization: str = '', client: str = '', summary: str = '', recommendations: Sequence[str] = (), sections: Sequence[str] | None = None, plugin_sections: Sequence[str] = ()) -> Report`

Write a report into ``<project>/reports`` from what the project holds.

Refused (with the checklist) when the project has nothing for this report type
to be about. ``plugin_sections`` appends sections built by installed
report-section plugins; one that fails is left out with a warning, never filled.

### `opendronekit.Refused`

*class* `opendronekit.Refused(reason: str, *, payload: dict | None = None)`

OpenDroneKit declined the request and said why.

The message is the same text the desktop application shows for the same refusal:
a missing dependency, an input that cannot support the result (an arbitrary-scale
model asked for metres, a photograph with no scale), a missing dataset, and so on.

### `opendronekit.Workspace`

*class* `opendronekit.Workspace(data_dir: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None)`

A folder holding OpenDroneKit projects, opened for scripting.

``data_dir`` is the same kind of folder as the application's data root
(``ODK_DATA_DIR``): the project index lives in ``<data_dir>/app_state/projects.db``
and new projects in ``<data_dir>/projects/<name>``. Pointing a workspace at the
application's own data root opens the user's real projects; point it at a scratch
folder for experiments.

#### `opendronekit.Workspace.close()`

Release the project index. The workspace cannot be used afterwards.

#### `opendronekit.Workspace.create_project(name: str, *, root: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None, description: str = '') -> 'Project'`

Create a project; refuses a name that already exists in this workspace.

#### `opendronekit.Workspace.open_project(project: int | str) -> 'Project'`

Open a project by numeric id or by (case-insensitive) name.

#### `opendronekit.Workspace.list_projects() -> list[ProjectInfo]`

Every project in this workspace.

#### `opendronekit.Workspace.capabilities() -> dict[str, Any]`

What this installation can actually do (the Environment Capabilities data).

#### `opendronekit.Workspace.mission_templates() -> list[str]`

Built-in planner templates plus installed mission-template plugins.

## opendronekit.plugins

The OpenDroneKit plugin API (contract level 1.1).

Plugins are ordinary Python distributions that declare an entry point in the
``opendronekit.plugins`` group. The entry point resolves to a :class:`PluginManifest`
(name, version, ``api_version``, and the plugins it provides)::

    # pyproject.toml of the plugin
    [project.entry-points."opendronekit.plugins"]
    corridor = "odk_corridor_template:manifest"

    # odk_corridor_template/__init__.py
    from opendronekit.plugins import PluginKind, PluginManifest, PluginSpec

    manifest = PluginManifest(
        name="odk-corridor-template", version="0.1.0", api_version="1.1",
        plugins=(PluginSpec(PluginKind.MISSION_TYPE, "corridor", CorridorTemplate),),
    )

Four kinds have a contract the host calls into; each is a small duck-typed object built
by the spec's factory:

==================  ===========================================================
Kind                What the built object must provide
==================  ===========================================================
``mission_type``    ``plan_options(aoi_lonlat, **params) -> dict`` (planner options;
                    may replace ``aoi_lonlat`` and must name a built-in ``template``)
``model``           ``model_key``, ``model_sha256`` and
                    ``detect(image_bgr) -> list[dict]`` (``label``, ``score``,
                    ``bbox_xyxy``)
``exporter``        ``suffix`` and ``export(plan: dict, path: Path) -> str | list[str]``
``report_section``  ``title`` and ``build(context: dict) -> dict`` (``paragraphs``
                    and/or ``table``)
==================  ===========================================================

The other kinds (drone, camera, payload, engine, report_template, map_provider) are
registered and listed the same way; their host integration is the factory call.

Failure isolation: discovery never raises for a broken plugin (it is listed under
``failed`` with the reason), and a plugin that raises or returns something outside its
contract raises :class:`PluginError` to the caller that asked for it -- never past it.
Output is checked, not trusted: an exporter that claims a file it did not write, a
detector with no model digest or a box outside the image, are refused.

| Constant | Value |
|---|---|
| `opendronekit.plugins.ENTRY_POINT_GROUP` | `'opendronekit.plugins'` |
| `opendronekit.plugins.PLUGIN_API_LEVEL` | `'1.1'` |
| `opendronekit.plugins.PLUGIN_API_VERSION` | `'1'` |

### `opendronekit.plugins.PluginHost`

*class* `opendronekit.plugins.PluginHost(plugin_registry: PluginRegistry | None = None)`

Loads plugins once, builds them on demand and checks what they return.

One process-wide instance, :data:`host`, backs the SDK, the desktop API's plugin
listing and Environment Capabilities. Tests make their own.

#### `opendronekit.plugins.PluginHost.load(*, refresh: bool = False, entry_points: Iterable[Any] | None = None) -> DiscoveryReport`

Discover installed plugins (once; ``refresh=True`` rescans).

#### `opendronekit.plugins.PluginHost.status() -> dict[str, Any]`

Loaded and failed plugins, for Environment Capabilities and ``list_plugins``.

#### `opendronekit.plugins.PluginHost.names(kind: PluginKind | str) -> list[str]`

Names of the loaded plugins of one kind.

#### `opendronekit.plugins.PluginHost.spec(kind: PluginKind | str, name: str) -> PluginSpec`

The loaded plugin's spec; :class:`PluginError` (stage ``lookup``) if none is installed.

#### `opendronekit.plugins.PluginHost.build(kind: PluginKind | str, name: str, **config: Any) -> tuple[PluginSpec, Any]`

The plugin object, built by its factory and checked against its contract.

#### `opendronekit.plugins.PluginHost.mission_options(name: str, aoi_lonlat: list[list[float]], **params: Any) -> dict[str, Any]`

Planner options from a mission-template plugin, validated.

#### `opendronekit.plugins.PluginHost.export(name: str, plan: dict[str, Any], directory: Path | str, stem: str = 'mission') -> list[Path]`

Run an exporter plugin; return the files it actually wrote.

#### `opendronekit.plugins.PluginHost.detect(name: str, image_bgr: Any) -> PluginDetections`

Run a detector plugin and refuse output that could not be traced or placed.

#### `opendronekit.plugins.PluginHost.report_section(name: str, context: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]`

A report block from a report-section plugin, given a copy of the context.

### `opendronekit.plugins.PluginKind`

str(object='') -> str
str(bytes_or_buffer[, encoding[, errors]]) -> str

Create a new string object from the given object. If encoding or
errors is specified, then the object must expose a data buffer
that will be decoded using the given encoding and error handler.
Otherwise, returns the result of object.__str__() (if defined)
or repr(object).
encoding defaults to sys.getdefaultencoding().
errors defaults to 'strict'.

| Member | Value |
|---|---|
| `DRONE` | `'drone'` |
| `CAMERA` | `'camera'` |
| `PAYLOAD` | `'payload'` |
| `MISSION_TYPE` | `'mission_type'` |
| `ENGINE` | `'engine'` |
| `MODEL` | `'model'` |
| `EXPORTER` | `'exporter'` |
| `REPORT_TEMPLATE` | `'report_template'` |
| `REPORT_SECTION` | `'report_section'` |
| `MAP_PROVIDER` | `'map_provider'` |

### `opendronekit.plugins.PluginManifest`

*dataclass* `opendronekit.plugins.PluginManifest(name: str, version: str, api_version: str, plugins: tuple[PluginSpec, ...], description: str = '', homepage: str = '', license: str = '')`

What one installed distribution provides: who it is and which plugins it adds.

An ``opendronekit.plugins`` entry point should resolve to one of these (or to a
zero-argument callable returning one). The manifest's ``api_version`` applies to
every plugin in it, and its ``version`` fills any plugin that does not state one.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str` | `required` |
| `version` | `str` | `required` |
| `api_version` | `str` | `required` |
| `plugins` | `tuple[PluginSpec, ...]` | `required` |
| `description` | `str` | `''` |

### `opendronekit.plugins.PluginRegistry`

*class* `opendronekit.plugins.PluginRegistry()`

Thread-safe explicit registry; importing the SDK performs no discovery or I/O.

#### `opendronekit.plugins.PluginRegistry.register(spec: PluginSpec, *, replace: bool = False) -> PluginSpec`

Add ``spec``; a name already taken in its kind raises unless ``replace``.

#### `opendronekit.plugins.PluginRegistry.unregister(kind: PluginKind | str, name: str)`

Remove a plugin; :class:`KeyError` if it is not registered.

#### `opendronekit.plugins.PluginRegistry.get(kind: PluginKind | str, name: str) -> PluginSpec`

The spec for ``kind``/``name``; :class:`KeyError` if it is not registered.

#### `opendronekit.plugins.PluginRegistry.has(kind: PluginKind | str, name: str) -> bool`

Whether ``kind``/``name`` is registered.

#### `opendronekit.plugins.PluginRegistry.create(kind: PluginKind | str, name: str, **configuration: Any) -> Any`

Build the plugin by calling its factory with ``configuration``.

#### `opendronekit.plugins.PluginRegistry.list(kind: PluginKind | str | None = None) -> list[PluginSpec]`

Registered specs, of one kind or of all kinds, sorted by kind and name.

#### `opendronekit.plugins.PluginRegistry.clear()`

Forget every registered plugin and recorded failure.

#### `opendronekit.plugins.PluginRegistry.load_manifest(path: str | Path, *, replace: bool = False) -> list[PluginSpec]`

Load explicitly selected local plugin factories from a versioned JSON file.

An explicit manifest is something the operator chose, so a bad one raises: the
mistake is theirs to see immediately. Installed entry points go through
:meth:`discover`, which never raises for a plugin's fault.

#### `opendronekit.plugins.PluginRegistry.discover(*, replace: bool = False, entry_points: Iterable[Any] | None = None) -> DiscoveryReport`

Load installed ``opendronekit.plugins`` entry points, skipping broken ones.

Each entry point may resolve to a :class:`PluginManifest`, a :class:`PluginSpec`,
a list of either, or a zero-argument callable returning one of those. Anything
that raises or does not fit is recorded in the report's ``failures`` and skipped;
this method does not raise for a plugin's fault.

#### `opendronekit.plugins.PluginRegistry.discover_entry_points(*, replace: bool = False) -> list[PluginSpec]`

Load installed ``opendronekit.plugins`` entry points only when requested.

Kept for code written against API 1.0. Broken plugins are skipped and listed in
``self.failures`` rather than raising; use :meth:`discover` for the full report.
